study.title: Effects of Acupuncture at Neiguan in Neural Activity of Related Brain Regions: A Resting-State fMRI Study in Anxiety
study.randomization: randomly divided into two groups according to a computer-generated random number table
study.blinding: single-blind; both groups did not know their grouping until the needling was performed
study.population: healthy right-handed volunteers with anxiety disorders; 20 to 35 years old postgraduates of Shandong Traditional Chinese Medicine University in China
study.inclusion_criteria: 20 to 35 years old; right-handed; anxiety disorders; SAS score 50 to 60
study.exclusion_criteria: with mental disorders; with major physical diseases; with contraindications for fMRI detection; with an acupuncture experience in the past week

conditions.scan_context: resting-state fMRI; participants requested to close their eyes, stay in stillness and avert emotional activities

conditions.timepoint_exact: after end of acupuncture; volunteer rests for 15 minutes and then undergoes an MRI

extraction_notes.note: The TR and TE parameters are reported as '3000 mm/35 mm' in the methods. The unit 'mm' for TR/TE is almost certainly a transcription or OCR error; these values should likely be in ms (3000 ms TR, 35 ms TE). Values preserved as reported.

Table 1: The left parahippocampal gyrus (59 voxels) and left fusiform gyrus (39 voxels) share a single peak coordinate (-33, -33, -18, T=6.9661). The table layout groups these two regions under the same peak, suggesting they belong to the same cluster or the fusiform gyrus has a separate unlisted peak. Extracted as separate rows per table structure.
Table 1: Right precuneus (161 voxels) and right cuneus (80 voxels) share a single peak coordinate (-9, -60, 45, T=-8.0823). Same issue as parahippocampal/fusiform pair above. Extracted accordingly.

Table 3: Several FC result rows (Right orbitofrontal back, 68 voxels; Fusiform gyrus, 73 voxels; Left gyrus angularis, 36 voxels) have no peak T value or coordinate reported in the table — they appear as sub-rows under other regions. Extracted with null coordinates and not_reported statistics.

The paper states ALFF was computed at '0.01–0.1 Hz' in the Data Pre-Processing section but '0.01–0.08 Hz' was used for temporal bandpass filtering. These two frequency ranges differ. Both values preserved as reported.
No post-acupuncture SAS scores are reported; no change from baseline in anxiety severity scores is quantified for either group.
Adverse events are not mentioned anywhere in the paper. Cannot confirm whether none occurred or whether reporting was omitted.
No expectancy, credibility, or treatment preference instruments were used or reported beyond the single-blind blinding statement.

Deqi sensation questionnaire results are only described narratively ('acupuncture at Neiguan obviously resulted in sensations compared to non-acupoint acupuncture'). No numerical scores, subscale values, or group statistics are provided.
Sex-stratified neuroimaging or clinical analyses are not performed; paper notes this as a limitation.
Trial registration number is not reported anywhere in the paper.

Flip angle (FA) reported as '90°' in sequence parameters. FOV is '230 mm × 230 mm'. Slice thickness/gap is '5.0 mm/0 mm'. Matrix is '128 × 128'. These are preserved in neuroimaging_methods via the sequence_exact field but not broken out individually.

The paper describes the two-sample t-test in the Analysis section for comparing groups, but the ALFF and FC results appear to be within-group pre vs post paired t-tests per the Data Pre-Processing section. Contrasts extracted as within-group paired t-tests consistent with the methods description.

The paper's conclusion references 'acupuncture of the Taichong point for the treatment of irritability and anxiety', which is inconsistent with the study's focus on Neiguan (PC6). This appears to be an error in the paper itself and is noted here.

Average ages reported as '25.6 ± 3.78 years for males and 26.1 ± 3.45 years for females (p < 0.05)'. The p < 0.05 for a non-significant or significant age difference between sexes is ambiguous in context.

The paper states 'The results were uncorrected with P < 0.01' for FC analysis, and separately 'P < 0.05 (uncorrected) and voxel range ≥10' for ALFF analysis. These two thresholds apply to different analyses and are preserved separately.
